title: Attack-Path Graph Visualization Foundation
goal: Turn the existing attack-path summary into a clearer relationship view without changing the attack-path data model or adding heavy graph dependencies by default.
scope: Add a first visual attack-path graph or structured relationship view inside the existing Surface / Attack Map using current attack-path API output, inventory, findings, and choke-point summaries. Keep the slice focused on visualization and explanation, not new inference, risk scoring, or identity-aware path expansion.
generation_reason: Backlog refresh requested by the project owner after the previous queue ended at backlog item 10.

constraints.active_task_gate: Do not implement this task until it is the single active task in NEXT_TASK.md.
constraints.scope_creep_guard: Only visualize existing attack-path API data. Defer new path inference, identity chaining, cloud chaining, and remediation-impact scoring.
notes: Prefer a dependency-free or very small rendering approach for this first slice.
Zero-data and low-confidence states must remain explicit.

success_criteria: Surface / Attack Map renders a clearer relationship view for existing candidate paths and choke points.
The graph or relationship view remains usable for zero-data, low-confidence, and multi-host runs.
Each visual path can be traced back to existing API output and evidence-backed finding/inventory records.
Browser coverage proves normal and empty-state rendering.
No new attack inference or scoring model is introduced.
must_not_touch: pack registry and runtime binding flows

acceptance_criteria: The view uses existing attack-path API output.
No graph view claims path certainty beyond the source confidence.
No identity-aware or cloud-aware inference is silently added.

before_promotion: The prior active task is completed and logged.
The existing attack-path summary API remains the source of truth.
after_completion: Update DONE_LOG.md with visualization changes and validation evidence.
Update CURRENT_STATE.md with the new attack-path visualization baseline and remaining graph gaps.
Promote exactly one next approved task package into NEXT_TASK.md, or set an explicit holding state if the queue is exhausted.
